question: Before judging whether an alum dose is adequate for a low alkalinity raw water, which input must the operator know first?
correctAnswer: The raw water alkalinity available to buffer the pH drop from alum dosing
explanation: Alum consumes alkalinity as it reacts, so the available alkalinity determines whether pH stays in a range where floc can form.
options: The finished water chlorine residual measured after the clearwell basin
The filter backwash volume recorded during the previous operating shift
The raw water alkalinity available to buffer the pH drop from alum dosing
The raw water temperature recorded at the intake structure last winter
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Coagulation chemistry and alkalinity. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The finished water chlorine residual measured after the clearwell basin
optionB: The filter backwash volume recorded during the previous operating shift
optionC: The raw water alkalinity available to buffer the pH drop from alum dosing
optionD: The raw water temperature recorded at the intake structure last winter

question: In a standard jar test sequence, which step immediately follows the rapid mix period?
correctAnswer: A slower flocculation mix that lets small floc particles grow larger
explanation: Rapid mix disperses the coagulant, then gentle slow mixing during flocculation lets destabilized particles collide and grow.
options: A slower flocculation mix that lets small floc particles grow larger
A settling period with the sample discarded and the jars refilled again
A filtration step through paper before any floc has time to develop
A chlorine dose added to disinfect the sample before it is measured
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Jar test dose selection. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: A slower flocculation mix that lets small floc particles grow larger
optionB: A settling period with the sample discarded and the jars refilled again
optionC: A filtration step through paper before any floc has time to develop
optionD: A chlorine dose added to disinfect the sample before it is measured

question: Tube settlers improve clarification mainly by changing which condition inside the settling basin?
correctAnswer: They shorten the distance a particle must settle to reach a surface
explanation: The closely spaced inclined tubes give particles a nearby surface to settle onto, so removal improves without enlarging the basin.
options: They raise the basin water temperature so particles become less dense
They shorten the distance a particle must settle to reach a surface
They add coagulant slowly along the full length of the settling basin
They deepen the basin so sludge can be stored for much longer periods
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Tube and plate settlers. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: They raise the basin water temperature so particles become less dense
optionB: They shorten the distance a particle must settle to reach a surface
optionC: They add coagulant slowly along the full length of the settling basin
optionD: They deepen the basin so sludge can be stored for much longer periods

question: In a dual media filter bed, how are the anthracite and sand layers normally arranged?
correctAnswer: Coarse light anthracite sits above finer denser sand in the bed
explanation: Coarser, lighter anthracite rests on finer, denser sand, so larger solids are caught up top and finer polishing happens below.
options: Fine dense sand sits above coarse light anthracite in the bed
Anthracite and sand are blended evenly throughout the whole bed
Coarse light anthracite sits above finer denser sand in the bed
A single mixed layer replaces both media after each backwash cycle
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Dual media filtration. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Fine dense sand sits above coarse light anthracite in the bed
optionB: Anthracite and sand are blended evenly throughout the whole bed
optionC: Coarse light anthracite sits above finer denser sand in the bed
optionD: A single mixed layer replaces both media after each backwash cycle

question: A clearwell has a baffling factor of 0.7. Applying that factor to the theoretical detention time produces which value?
correctAnswer: The effective contact time credited for disinfection in the clearwell
explanation: The baffling factor corrects theoretical detention time for short circuiting, giving the effective contact time used for CT credit.
options: The effective contact time credited for disinfection in the clearwell
The total time treated water spends travelling through the distribution system
The time required to fill the clearwell from empty at the design flow rate
The average age of water stored in the clearwell since the last cleaning
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources

optionB: The total time treated water spends travelling through the distribution system
optionC: The time required to fill the clearwell from empty at the design flow rate
optionD: The average age of water stored in the clearwell since the last cleaning

question: On a breakpoint chlorination curve, what happens to the combined chlorine residual as the dose rises toward the breakpoint?
correctAnswer: It falls as the chloramines are oxidized and destroyed by the chlorine
explanation: Between the hump and the dip of the curve, added chlorine oxidizes chloramines, so the combined residual falls toward the breakpoint.
options: It rises steadily until free chlorine appears in the finished water
It stays unchanged because chloramines do not react with added chlorine
It falls as the chloramines are oxidized and destroyed by the chlorine
It converts directly into chloride before any chlorine demand is exerted
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Breakpoint chlorination. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: It rises steadily until free chlorine appears in the finished water
optionB: It stays unchanged because chloramines do not react with added chlorine
optionC: It falls as the chloramines are oxidized and destroyed by the chlorine
optionD: It converts directly into chloride before any chlorine demand is exerted

question: Which storage condition applies to bags of dry treatment chemical kept in the plant chemical room?
correctAnswer: Keep bags dry, off the floor, and away from incompatible chemicals
explanation: Dry chemicals stay usable and safe when kept dry, raised off the floor, and separated from chemicals they could react with.

Keep bags dry, off the floor, and away from incompatible chemicals
Store the bags outdoors uncovered so any spills wash away in rain
Keep bags in the warmest room available to speed up later dissolving

question: After a storm, raw turbidity doubles and the operator raises the alum dose. The settled water pH then falls and floc becomes weak. What is the most likely cause and the best next check?
correctAnswer: The extra alum consumed alkalinity the raw water did not have; check alkalinity and jar test a supplemental alkalinity dose
explanation: Higher alum doses consume more alkalinity, and a low alkalinity water cannot buffer the drop, so pH falls and floc formation suffers.
options: The extra alum consumed alkalinity the raw water did not have; check alkalinity and jar test a supplemental alkalinity dose
The filters are passing solids back into the basin; check the backwash valves and recycle the settled water to the intake
The raw water temperature fell too quickly overnight; check the intake heaters and raise the rapid mix speed for one hour
The alum has expired in storage and lost all strength; check the delivery date and double the dose until floc improves

optionB: The filters are passing solids back into the basin; check the backwash valves and recycle the settled water to the intake
optionC: The raw water temperature fell too quickly overnight; check the intake heaters and raise the rapid mix speed for one hour

question: A jar test series gives settled turbidity of 8, 4, 1.8 and 3.5 NTU at doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg/L. The plant target for settled water is below 2 NTU. Which dose should the operator select?

The 40 mg/L dose, because the highest dose tested gives the widest safety margin for storms

question: During a media top up, a contractor places new sand above the anthracite by mistake and the filter is returned to service. Which consequence is most likely?
correctAnswer: Fine sand on top strains solids at the surface, so head loss builds quickly and runs shorten sharply

The filter produces lower turbidity for much longer runs because the finest media now contacts water first
The anthracite below dissolves slowly into the sand layer and the two media become one uniform material

question: Raw water ammonia rises after spring runoff. The chlorine dose is unchanged, free residual disappears, and combined residual climbs. What adjustment fits this change?

Raise the chlorine dose toward the breakpoint to satisfy the added ammonia demand
Stop chlorination until the ammonia passes through the plant on its own
Add the same dose twice as fast so the contact time in the pipe is halved

question: A filter shows a turbidity spike in the first minutes of every run, then long periods of excellent quality. The plant has a filter to waste line that is rarely used. Which operating decision fits the evidence?

question: The operator raises the chlorine dose in steps, yet free residual stays at zero while combined residual keeps falling. A feeder check shows the pump is delivering correctly. Which interpretation best fits the readings?
correctAnswer: The water is still before the breakpoint, with chlorine consumed destroying chloramines as the dose climbs
explanation: Falling combined residual with no free residual is the dip region of the breakpoint curve; the dose has not yet passed the breakpoint.

The chlorine has expired in storage, and expired chlorine lowers combined residual without exerting any demand
The ammonia has been fully removed already, so the remaining chlorine demand must come from the filter media itself
